newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZFOE to launch monthly electricity futures in Nov.
newsitem.headline: NZFOE to launch monthly electricity futures in Nov.

text.p: The New Zealand Futures and Options Exchange on Wednesday said it hoped to launch a monthly electricity futures contract in November of this year.
"The final date will be decided in the next few days," Greg Boland, manager of the exchange's business development unit, told Reuters.
New Zealand's new wholesale electricity market officially began on Tuesday.

Boland said a monthly futures contract had been favoured over a weekly contract for two reasons: "One was liquidity, and the second is technically -- there's no futures contracts anywhere in the world which are weekly," Boland said.
He dismissed a suggestion by an electricity market analyst that a weekly contract would be more useful in the new electricity market, saying it was essentially the same thing.
"Isn't it? Isn't four one-weekly contracts the same as a monthly contract?" he asked.
"Bank bills are traded every day but bank bill futures are traded on a three-monthly basis."
He said the monthly contract had been decided upon primarily for liquidity reasons.
